_about: Card text for the project page. build.py lists every skill in .claude/skills/; this file only gives each one a group, a one-line summary, a 'just say' example and an optional badge. A skill missing here still appears, under 'More', with the first sentence of its own description.

groups.title: Cut
groups.blurb: From raw take to a clean first cut.

groups.title: Fill
groups.blurb: B-roll, graphics and the lines you forgot to say.

groups.title: Polish
groups.blurb: Notes, drafts, audio and shaky shots.

groups.title: Ship
groups.blurb: Everything YouTube asks for, ready to paste.

groups.title: Home videos
groups.blurb: The trip, the dog, the birthday. Not for the channel.

groups.title: Keep it tidy
groups.blurb: Footage in, projects out, drive space back.

aroll-draft.line: Raw talking-head take in, first cut out. Retakes, false starts, mic checks and filler gone, every cut snapped to the waveform so no word gets clipped.

multicam-angles.line: Shot with two cameras? Picks the angle for every cut, adds a face picture-in-picture where you show things, and stops the flicker.

talking-head-ffmpeg.line: The whole edit with no editing app: your cut plus b-roll as one JSON recipe that ffmpeg renders.
talking-head-ffmpeg.say: edit this with b-roll, no Resolve

unboxing-cut.line: A long overhead unboxing becomes a paced, ASMR-style sequence: the box, the knife, the peel, the reveal.

broll-brick-layer.line: Looks at your b-roll, matches shots to what you're saying, lays them on the timeline, then a second agent tries to veto every one.

broll-library.line: Every clip you've shot, described and searchable. Harvest the b-roll from finished edits and find it again next year.
broll-library.say: have I ever shot a rainy street?

motion-graphics.line: Animated stats, charts, callouts and lower thirds timed to your words, in your colours, rendered with the browser you already have.

vo-gapfill.line: Missing a sentence? Writes the line in your on-camera voice and fills the gap with your own text-to-speech voice.
vo-gapfill.say: do a voiceover for that gap

camera-ab-compare.line: Two phones, one walk: works out which phone shot what, pairs matching moments and builds the side-by-side.
camera-ab-compare.say: compare these two phones side by side

edit-review-notes.line: Watch the draft, type or dictate notes in EditReview as you go, and Claude applies them. The next draft shows only what changed.

resolve-export-draft.line: A review draft of your Resolve timeline, rendered from the command line. No Deliver page.

voice-clear.line: Takes the room echo and noise out of your voice, on your Mac, only when you ask.

stabilize-clips.line: Smooths shaky handheld clips, measures whether it helped, and keeps the original when it didn't.

ship-it.line: Two words from approved draft to ready to upload: master, loudness, title, chapters, thumbnails and a paste sheet.

youtube-release.line: Title options in your style, a description with chapters and your links, and loudness fixed for YouTube.

youtube-thumbnails.line: Thumbnails from your real footage, with the hook lifted from your own words, checked for privacy and legibility.

studio-thumbnails.line: Adds AI concepts from YouTube Studio's Ask Studio and Gemini to the pool, next to the real-footage ones.

shorts.line: Finds Shorts in your finished video, word-precise with a hook in the first two seconds, reframed for 9:16 and captioned.

home-video.line: A trip, pet or family montage from a pile of phone clips, scored with music. A privacy mode keeps every frame on your Mac.
home-video.say: make a video of our trip

montage-music.line: Picks tracks you have the rights to, finds the beats and the right place to start, and mixes them under the clips.
montage-music.say: pick a song for this part

footage-triage.line: Sorts an import dump into projects, the home-video archive, the b-roll library or the trash. You approve every move.

archive-project.line: Done with a video? Keeps the finals and the good b-roll and clears the rest. Dry run first, copy and verify before any delete.

new-project.line: A new project folder in your own layout, ready for footage.
new-project.say: start a new project called Backpack review

setup.line: About ten minutes of skippable questions, and every skill knows where your stuff lives.

customize.line: Say "from now on..." once and it remembers. Or ask it to change any skill, or write you a new one.
customize.say: from now on, keep my jokes

editing-coach.line: Learning to edit? J-cuts, pacing, colour in Resolve, stop motion, and feedback on your own clips.
editing-coach.say: how do I color correct in Resolve?

aroll-benchmark.line: For tinkerers: scores the automatic cut against your own edit of the same take.
aroll-benchmark.say: score the auto cut against my edit
